items.q: Cūr ōlim nēmō sine maximō perīculō nāvigābat?
items.en: Why did no one once sail without the greatest danger?
answers: quia cūncta maria tam infēsta erant praedōnibus
quod cūncta maria infēsta erant praedōnibus
cūncta maria tam infēsta erant praedōnibus ut nēmō sine perīculō nāvigāret
items.hint: a result clause: tam … ut + imperfect subjunctive; infēstus takes the dative (praedōnibus)

items.q: Quī sōlī servitūte līberābantur?
items.en: Who alone were freed from slavery?
answers: iī quī magnam pecūniam solvere potuerant
choices: iī quī magnam pecūniam solvere potuerant
items.hint: a relative clause as subject (pluperfect potuerant); servitūte is an ablative of separation

items.q: Quandō Caesar ā praedōnibus captus est?
items.en: When was Caesar captured by pirates?
answers: cum adulēscēns ex Italiā Rhodum nāvigāret
cum adulēscēns ex Italiā Rhodum nāvigāret captus est
items.hint: a circumstantial cum clause with the imperfect subjunctive; Rhodum is an island name in the accusative (place to which)

items.q: Cūr parum frūmentī ex Siciliā et ex Āfricā Rōmam advehēbātur?
items.en: Why was too little grain being brought to Rome from Sicily and Africa?
answers: quoniam propter praedōnēs nē mare Tūscum quidem tūtum erat
quoniam nē mare Tūscum quidem tūtum erat
quia propter vim atque multitūdinem praedōnum nē mare Tūscum quidem tūtum erat
choices: quoniam propter praedōnēs nē mare Tūscum quidem tūtum erat
quoniam Sicilia et Āfrica dēsertae erant
quoniam classis Rōmāna in Asiā erat
items.hint: a quoniam clause; propter + accusative gives the cause; parum takes a partitive genitive (frūmentī)

items.q: Quid populus Rōmānus ūnō ōre postulāvit?
items.en: What did the Roman people demand with one voice?
answers: ut ūniversa classis Rōmāna adversus praedōnēs mitterētur
ut ūniversa classis Rōmāna adversus hostēs illōs audācissimōs mitterētur
items.hint: postulāvit ut + imperfect subjunctive passive (mitterētur); the cum clause before it is causal

items.q: Quis classī Rōmānae praepositus est?
items.en: Who was put in charge of the Roman fleet?
items.hint: the nominative subject; classī is a dative with praepōnere

items.q: Quōmodo cūnctus populus Rōmānus Pompēium victōrem affēcit?
items.en: How did the whole Roman people treat the victorious Pompey?
items.hint: afficere takes an ablative (summīs laudibus = with the highest praise)

items.q: Quid ex eō tempore rārō fit?
items.en: What rarely happens from that time on?
answers: ut nāvis praedōnum in marī Internō appāreat
choices: ut nāvis praedōnum in marī Internō appāreat
items.hint: fit ut + present subjunctive ('it happens that')

items.q: Quantā audāciā sunt praedōnēs quī adhūc supersunt?
items.en: How bold are the pirates who still remain?
answers: tantā audāciā ut nē armīs quidem Rōmānōrum dēterreantur
tantā ut nē armīs quidem dēterreantur
tantā audāciā sunt ut nē armīs quidem Rōmānōrum dēterreantur
tantā audāciā ut nē armīs quidem dēterreantur
items.hint: an ablative of description (tantā audāciā) followed by a result clause with the present subjunctive

items.q: Quid gubernātor caelum suspiciēns optat?
items.en: What does the helmsman wish for as he looks up at the sky?
answers: optat ut ventus in adversum vertātur
items.hint: optat ut + present subjunctive passive (a wish)

items.q: Quālēs nautās suōs gubernātor esse crēdit?
items.en: What kind of men does the helmsman believe his sailors to be?
items.hint: an accusative adjective in an indirect statement (nautās … validōs esse), followed by a result clause tam … ut

items.q: Quid Mēdus adhūc sub veste occultāvit?
items.en: What has Medus been hiding under his clothing?
items.hint: the accusative object of ēdūcit and occultāvit; occīdar is a future passive

items.q: Quōmodo perībunt omnēs quī gladium cēperint, ut Chrīstus ait?
items.en: How will all who take the sword perish, as Christ says?
items.hint: an ablative of means; cēperint is a future perfect in the relative clause

items.q: Quid gubernātor Mēdō dissuādēre cōnātur?
items.en: What does the helmsman try to dissuade Medus from?
answers: nē gladium ēdūcat neu praedōnibus resistat
nē gladium ēdūcat neu praedōnibus vī et armīs resistat
nē praedōnibus vī et armīs resistat
items.hint: dissuādēre nē … neu + present subjunctive; resistere takes the dative (praedōnibus)

items.q: Cūr praedōnēs nautās inermēs nōn occīdunt?
items.en: Why don't pirates kill unarmed sailors?
answers: cum eōs magnō pretiō servōs vēndere possint
quia eōs magnō pretiō servōs vēndere possunt
items.hint: a causal cum clause with the present subjunctive (possint); magnō pretiō is an ablative of price

items.q: Quot mīlia sēstertium gubernātor praedōnibus offerre potest?
items.en: How many thousand sesterces can the helmsman offer the pirates?
items.hint: mīlia takes a genitive plural (sēstertium = sēstertiōrum)

items.q: Quibus fortūnā adversā fīdendum nōn est?
items.en: Whom must one not trust when fortune is against you?
items.hint: fīdere takes the dative; fīdendum est is an impersonal gerundive ('one must trust')

items.q: Quandō sōlus eris, ut Ovidius scrīpsit?
items.en: When will you be alone, as Ovid wrote?
items.hint: sī + future perfect (fuerint) with a future main verb

items.q: Quis illōs versūs scrīpsit, nisi memoria mercātōrem fallit?
items.en: Who wrote those verses, unless the merchant's memory fails him?
items.hint: the nominative subject of scrīpsit

items.q: Utrum facilius est: grātiās agere an beneficiōrum meminisse?
items.en: Which is easier: to give thanks or to remember kindnesses?
items.hint: infinitive phrases as subjects; meminisse takes the genitive (beneficiōrum)

items.q: Quid gubernātor mīrātur?
items.en: What does the helmsman wonder about?
answers: unde Mēdus pecūniam sūmpserit ut aliōs redimeret
unde pecūniam sūmpserit ut aliōs redimeret
items.hint: an indirect question with the perfect subjunctive (sūmpserīs), followed by a purpose clause (ut … redimerēs)

items.q: Cūr Mēdus nihil cuiquam dē eā rē nārrāvit?
items.en: Why did Medus tell no one about that matter?
items.hint: a negative purpose clause: nē + imperfect subjunctive; quis after nē = 'anyone'

items.q: Ubi Mēdus homō līber vīvēbat?
items.en: Where did Medus live as a free man?
items.hint: a city name in the ablative/locative for place where (no preposition)

items.q: Quid amīcus Mēdum per amīcitiam ōrāvit?
items.en: What did the friend beg Medus, by their friendship, to do?
answers: ut sē ē servitūte redimeret magnum pretium solvendō
items.hint: ōrāvit ut + imperfect subjunctive; solvendō is a gerund in the ablative ('by paying')

items.q: Cūr homō dīves Mēdum in carcerem mīsit?
items.en: Why did the rich man send Medus to prison?
answers: quia pecūniam dēbitam solvere nōn poterat
cum pecūniam dēbitam solvere nōn posset
quod pecūniam dēbitam solvere nōn poterat
choices: quia pecūniam dēbitam solvere nōn poterat
items.hint: a causal cum clause with the imperfect subjunctive (nōn posset); diē … cōnstitūtā is an ablative absolute

items.q: Quid Mēdus sibi optat?
items.en: What does Medus wish for himself?
items.hint: utinam + present subjunctive expresses a wish for the future

items.q: Quōmodo Mēdus sē redimere fortasse poterit, ut gubernātor dīcit?
items.en: How might Medus be able to ransom himself, according to the helmsman?
items.hint: an ablative of means; the sentence before uses nē + perfect subjunctive for a prohibition (nē dēspērāverīs)

items.q: Quot talenta pīrātae ā Caesare captō postulāvērunt?
items.en: How many talents did the pirates demand from the captured Caesar?
items.hint: a numeral in the accusative (indeclinable); id est introduces the sum in sesterces

items.q: Quid Caesar praedōnibus quasi servīs suīs imperāvit?
items.en: What did Caesar order the pirates, as if they were his slaves, to do?
answers: ut tacērent neu somnum suum turbārent
ut tacērent neu somnum eius turbārent
choices: ut tacērent neu somnum suum turbārent
items.hint: imperāvit ut … neu + imperfect subjunctive; cum … esset is a concessive cum clause

items.q: Quō Caesar captōs praedōnēs tollī iussit?
items.en: Where did Caesar order the captured pirates to be raised?
items.hint: in + accusative; tollī is a passive infinitive after iussit; ubi prīmum + perfect

items.q: Quae hōc ānulō servanda est, ut Mēdus dīcit?
items.en: Who must be saved by this ring, according to Medus?
items.hint: a gerundive with est (servanda est = must be saved) agreeing with a feminine subject

items.q: Quid Mēdus ā Lydiā rogat?
items.en: What does Medus ask of Lydia?
answers: ut sē amet ita ut eum amābat
ut mē amēs ita ut mē amābās
nihil nisi ut eum amet ita ut eum amābat
items.hint: nihil … nisi ut + present subjunctive (an indirect command)

items.q: Laetāturne Mēdus quod cēterī ē perīculō servātī sunt?
items.en: Is Medus glad that the others have been saved from danger?
answers: Ita, laetātur sānē quod servātī sunt
Laetātur sānē quod vōs servātī estis
items.hint: a yes/no question with -ne; laetārī is deponent, and quod + indicative gives the cause; aequē … atque = 'as much as'

items.q: Quid Mēdus timet?
items.en: What does Medus fear?
answers: nē mīlitēs sē captum Rōmam abdūcant
nē mīlitēs eum captum Rōmam abdūcant
nē mīlitēs mē captum Rōmam abdūcant
nē Rōmam abdūcātur et ad bēstiās mittātur
choices: nē mīlitēs sē captum Rōmam abdūcant
items.hint: a fear clause: timeō nē + present subjunctive (the ut clause after it is purpose)

items.q: Quālem nāvem esse mīlitēs cognōscunt?
items.en: What kind of ship do the soldiers recognise it to be?
items.hint: an accusative adjective in an indirect statement, inside a result clause (tam prope … ut + present subjunctive)

items.q: Cūr nymphae silvās et flūminis aquās relinquēbant?
items.en: Why did the nymphs leave the woods and the river waters?
answers: ut mīrābilia opera ab Arachnē cōnfecta aspicerent
ut mīrābilia opera ab eā cōnfecta aspicerent
items.hint: a purpose clause: ut + imperfect subjunctive

items.q: Quid Minerva timet, ut Arachnē dīcit?
items.en: What does Minerva fear, according to Arachne?
items.hint: a fear clause: timet nē + present subjunctive passive

items.q: Cūr nymphae perterritae fūgērunt?
items.en: Why did the terrified nymphs flee?
answers: timentēs nē ipsae ā deā īrātā poenā afficerentur
quia timēbant nē ā deā īrātā poenā afficerentur
quia timēbant nē ipsae poenā afficerentur
items.hint: a fear clause after a participle: timentēs nē + imperfect subjunctive; poenā is an ablative with afficere

items.q: Quid Minerva Arachnae optat?
items.en: What does Minerva wish for Arachne?
items.hint: utinam + present subjunctive (a wish); verērī is a deponent infinitive

items.q: Utra melius opus fēcisse intellegēbātur?
items.en: Which of the two was understood to have made the better work?
items.hint: the Greek accusative subject of an indirect statement (Arachnēn … fēcisse); dubitāvit num introduces an indirect question

items.q: Quōmodo Arachnē arānea facta est?
items.en: How was Arachne turned into a spider?
answers: Minerva eam herbae cuiusdam sūcō aspersit
items.hint: an ablative of means; quō factum est ut + imperfect subjunctive is a result clause
